problem: Future-prediction curiosity (ICM, large-scale curiosity, disagreement) is hard to train and is fooled by stochasticity (couch-potato / noisy-TV problem). Prior audio-visual navigation work needs an explicit goal and reward, so there is no unsupervised way to use audio for exploration.
motivation: Humans explore by seeking novel cross-modal associations (sight plus sound), and audio and vision arise from the same physical processes. Classifying whether an image and a sound are aligned is a simpler, binary problem than predicting future observations, and it ignores random stochasticity. This could give a more robust intrinsic reward.
key_idea: Train an online discriminator to tell aligned from misaligned (image, audio) pairs, and reward the agent with the discriminator's negative log-likelihood on the true pair, so it seeks novel audio-visual associations.
insight: Association is a more robust novelty signal than future prediction. Adding audio to the prediction and RND baselines (concatenated features) gives no real gain, so the benefit comes from the association objective and not from extra information. With Gaussian noise added to features, future-prediction curiosity degrades on Asterix and SpaceInvaders while SHE stays stable. Failure cases occur when the association is trivial (Qbert, Atlantis) or the audio is repetitive background sound that cannot be aligned visually (SpaceInvaders, BeamRider, Alien).
method: Alignment discriminator: MLP with 2×512 hidden layers and a single sigmoid output; it takes a 512-d visual feature and a 512-d audio feature and predicts whether they are aligned.

Negative sampling: with probability 0.5 the true audio is replaced by audio sampled uniformly from the same 128-step trajectory. The negative cross-entropy term is weighted by the normalized L2 distance between true and false audio, so similar sounds are not penalized.
Intrinsic reward: r_t = -log D(v_t, s_t). Aligned pairs the discriminator already knows give zero reward; surprising pairs give high reward. The agent only observes vision, not audio.
Features: fixed random-weight CNN for vision (84x84x4 grayscale stack) and FFT with max-pool downsampling to 512-d for audio (Atari clip spans 4 timesteps; Habitat clip is 1 s zero-padded).
Policy learning: PPO on intrinsic reward only, with no extrinsic reward; 128 parallel environments in Atari, 1 in Habitat; hyperparameters copied from large-scale curiosity.
Joint variant: sum the future-prediction and SHE intrinsic losses/rewards to combine complementary curiosities.

setting.backbone: PPO policy with fixed random CNN visual features; audio-visual discriminator (MLP) trained online from scratch
setting.training_data: None beyond online self-collected exploration: 200M frames per Atari game with intrinsic reward only; Habitat trained online in a single Replica scene
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB frames (grayscale 84x84, 4-frame stack) for the policy; audio (FFT) used only by the reward model
setting.action_space: Habitat: 3 discrete actions (turn left, turn right, move forward) on a grid of 211 locations x 4 headings; Atari: Discrete(6)
setting.simulator: Habitat (Replica Apartment 0 with SoundSpaces-style audio from Chen et al.) and Gym Retro Atari
setting.privileged: none at test time; extrinsic reward is used only for evaluation; audio is used only to compute the training reward

numbers_note: Results are given only in figures (Atari training curves, Habitat state coverage and count plots); no tables. Text-only figures: SHE beats disagreement in 9/12 and future prediction in 8/12 Atari games; in Alien, joint method 593 vs SHE 108 vs future prediction 359 (average final extrinsic reward, not a navigation benchmark).
results: On Atari, SHE outperforms the future-prediction baseline in 8 of 12 games and disagreement in 9 of 12, and it is the only method to make progress on the hard-exploration game Gravitar. In Habitat (Replica Apartment 0), SHE reaches full state coverage about 3x faster than future-prediction curiosity (similar to RND) and visits rare states about 8x more often than the next-best baseline. It is also more robust to noise, and combining it with future prediction beats future prediction alone in 10 of 12 games.
limitations: Fails when audio-visual association is trivial (Qbert, Atlantis) or audio is repetitive or hard to align (SpaceInvaders, BeamRider, Alien).
Habitat evaluation is a single small scene with a fixed audio source, and it measures only state coverage (no navigation task metrics); results appear only in figures with 3 seeds.
Requires an informative audio channel; a learning agent might exploit the reward, for example by repeating a delayed-sound trick.
